      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could read the key through csr_rdata_o or overwrite a key word through the CSR write path.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "csr_wdata_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "csr_rdata_o",
        "result_o"
      ],

The operand registers are loaded from rs1_i and rs2_i at lines 205-206, so changing the captured values changes the cryptographic operation.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter or observe the operand values supplied to the custom instruction and thereby obtain or corrupt the processed data.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "rs1_i",
        "rs2_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "result_o"

conceptual assets.information: The four-word key used by the XTEA computation is stored in the internal key memory. Correct encryption or decryption depends on this key material.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The key can be exposed through the CSR readback at line 185 and can also influence the returned result through lines 236-249. The key memory can be overwritten when csr_we_i is asserted at lines 178-179, allowing unauthorized key modification.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read the key through csr_rdata_o or overwrite a key word through the CSR write path.

conceptual assets.information: The two 32-bit operand words form the data block processed by the XTEA operation. The custom instruction depends on capturing and using these operand values correctly.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The operands may contain sensitive plaintext or ciphertext and are held in xtea.opa and xtea.opb at lines 205-206 before influencing the returned result through lines 232-249. The operand registers are loaded from rs1_i and rs2_i at lines 205-206, so changing the captured values changes the cryptographic operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter or observe the operand values supplied to the custom instruction and thereby obtain or corrupt the processed data.

conceptual assets.information: The XTEA result word is computed from the operands and selected key word. Correct custom-instruction execution depends on returning this transformed data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The computed cryptographic result is observable at result_o on line 249. xtea.res is recomputed from tmp_b and tmp_r on lines 222 and 224, so corruption of the operands, key, or arithmetic path changes the returned result. The result transfer can be withheld by the valid and operation-selection logic on lines 245-256 and 261-262.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the arithmetic inputs or prevent valid_o from qualifying the result, causing disclosure, an incorrect result, or a lost result transfer.

conceptual assets.information: The start command requests capture of the operands and initiation of a custom XTEA operation. Operation progress depends on this command being accepted.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The start_i condition at line 204 controls operand capture and the initial done indication, so the internal operation can be prevented from starting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or improperly gate start_i so that the coprocessor does not capture operands or produce a result.

conceptual assets.information: The completion status indicates whether result_o contains a valid custom-operation result. The receiving processor depends on this status to accept or wait for the result.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: valid_o is produced from the operation completion state and instruction selection at lines 250-256 and 262, so an incorrect status can cause an invalid result to be accepted or a valid result to be withheld. The same assignments can keep the result transfer unavailable by leaving valid_o low.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could induce a false or missing valid indication, causing the processor to consume invalid data or lose a completed result.

conceptual assets.information: The CSR write-enable and address controls select and initiate programming or reading of a key-memory word. Key provisioning depends on this access command being accepted.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: csr_we_i gates the key-memory write at line 178 and csr_addr_i selects the accessed word at lines 179 and 185, so the internal access path can withhold required key provisioning.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress the write command or steer it to an unintended key-memory entry, preventing required key configuration.
